question.worked_solution:
First, we multiply both sides of the equation by $7$ to get rid of the fraction:

$$
\begin{aligned}\begin{aligned}\frac{3}{7}x & =6 \\ 7\cdot \frac{3}{7}x & =7\cdot 6 \\ \cancel{7}\cdot \frac{3}{\cancel{7}}x & =7\cdot 6 \\ 3x & =42\end{aligned}\end{aligned}
$$

Then, we divide both sides of the equation by $3$ to isolate $x:$

$$
\begin{aligned}\begin{aligned}3x & =42 \\ \frac{3x}{3} & =\frac{42}{3} \\ \frac{\cancel{3}x}{\cancel{3}} & =\frac{42}{3} \\ x & =14\end{aligned}\end{aligned}
$$
